# Reproducibility {#sec-reproducibility}

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
source("_common.R")
```

Anyone who runs this book should get the same numbers. Three things make that possible.

## The same packages: renv

R packages change between versions, and a new version can change a result. The
[renv](https://rstudio.github.io/renv/) package records the exact version of every package
the book uses in `renv.lock` and installs those versions into a library inside the project
(`renv/library/`), separate from your other R projects.

| Task | Command (R console, in the project) |
|---|---|
| Install the recorded versions (once, after downloading the project) | `renv::restore()` |
| Check that the installed packages match the lockfile | `renv::status()` |
| After adding a package to `DESCRIPTION` and installing it | `renv::snapshot()` |

`renv` starts automatically when R opens in the project folder (through the `.Rprofile`
file). The packages the book needs are listed in `DESCRIPTION`; `renv` records them and their
dependencies.

## The same random numbers: seeds

Multiple imputation draws random values. `_common.R` sets the same seed (`r seed`) at the
start of every chapter. The imputation runs one task per imputation in parallel, and
`furrr::furrr_options(seed = seed)` gives each task its own reproducible random-number stream,
so the imputed values are the same whether your computer has 2 cores or 16.

## Smoke tests

A full render takes time because of the imputation. Before a full run, a smoke test checks
that every chapter works:

```sh
quarto render book --profile smoke
```

The `smoke` profile (`_quarto-smoke.yml` and `_environment-smoke`) sets the number of
imputations to 2 and writes the book to `book/_book-smoke/` and the data to
`data/processed-smoke/`. Every page of a smoke book says "SMOKE TEST" in its title. The
number of imputations is set in one place (`N_IMPUTATIONS`, read in `_common.R`), and every
count in the code and text follows it.

## Reusing expensive calculations

Expensive R chunks use `#| cache: true`, Quarto's standard knitr cache. The
setup records the chapter's R code, contents of its input files, shared settings,
R/package versions and survey options in `cache.extra`. These inputs invalidate
cached results when the analysis changes. Editing prose does not.

Full runs store their caches in `data/processed/cache/`; smoke runs use
`data/processed-smoke/cache/`. Setup and file-saving chunks always run, so later
chapters still receive their inputs on a cached render. Only rendering uses the
cache; running individual lines in the R console executes them normally.

To recalculate all cached chunks:

```sh
quarto render book --cache-refresh
```

Or refresh only the descriptive chapter:

```sh
quarto render book/03-descriptives.qmd --cache-refresh
```

See the [Quarto caching documentation](https://quarto.org/docs/computations/caching.html)
for details. Validate the initial calculation before relying on cached results.

## Session information

The R version, operating system, and package versions used for this render:

```{r}
#| label: session-info
utils::sessionInfo()
```
